stem: A $0.20\ \text{m}$ aqueous solution of $\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4$ freezes at $-0.744^\circ\text{C}$. Find its degree of dissociation, given $K_f=1.86\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.
working:
$i=\dfrac{\Delta T_f}{K_fm}=\dfrac{0.744}{1.86\times0.20}=2$


Independent check: \(\Delta T_f=iK_fm\), so \(i=0.744/(1.86\times0.20)=2\). For \(\mathrm{K_2SO_4\to2K^++SO_4^{2-}}\), \(i=1+2\alpha\), giving \(\alpha=0.50\).
solution:
For $\mathrm{K_2SO_4 \to 2K^+ + SO_4^{2-}}$, the van’t Hoff factor is $i=1+2\alpha$.
$$i=\frac{\Delta T_f}{K_fm}=\frac{0.744}{1.86\times0.20}=2$$
Thus, $2=1+2\alpha$, so $\alpha=0.50=50\%$.
